editorial:
If you love a mystery that unfolds entirely through screens, Missing pulls you in fast. June is a teen in Los Angeles whose mom vanishes during a Colombia trip with her new boyfriend. Stuck at home, she uses phones, cameras, apps, and online records to track clues. The story feels modern and tense, turning everyday tech into a detective tool. Storm Reid gives June a believable mix of fear, stubbornness, and heart, while the plot keeps throwing new twists at you. It is a smart, screen-based thriller that makes you want to lean closer.

The pacing rarely slows, and the digital clues are fun to follow, though some twists may feel a bit much if you prefer grounded stories. Still, the movie delivers strong suspense, emotional family drama, and a satisfying payoff. It is best for viewers who enjoy tech-driven mysteries, teen-led thrillers, and fast plots.
endingExplained: By the end, June discovers that her mother’s boyfriend Kevin is actually her father, James, who faked his death and kidnapped Grace to lure June to Colombia. June follows digital clues to their location, confronts him, and Grace fights back during the rescue. James is killed, and June and Grace finally reunite, facing the painful family secrets they had hidden from each other.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves screen-based mysteries and family thrillers.
